decisions.reason: Step 1.1 used the Darboux FTC directly inside Lebesgue Holder estimates. Added the continuous-integrability and Riemann–Lebesgue equality suppliers, extended the test function smoothly by zero to the endpoints, and explicitly transferred the derivative integral before applying Holder. Closure approximation controls both L2 components within epsilon and yields the stated norm bounds; the Statement is unchanged.

A C1 diffeomorphism need not make B_h bounded: Phi(y)=log(y), A=1 gives B_h=y. Already v(y)=log(1+y) has square-integrable gradient on (0,infinity) but infinite B_h-energy, since y/(1+y)^2 has divergent integral. Defined the lifted form on finite-energy pairs, with weighted Cauchy–Schwarz and Holder guaranteeing an integrable cross density; form defects require both cross densities integrable. Retained arbitrary diffeomorphisms and the tensor formula, and carried the existing change-of-variables Countable Choice assumption explicitly.

The discrete map was only required to satisfy a bound and diagonal coercivity. On R, a_h(v,w)=c(v)vw with c(v)=1 for |v|<=1 and 2 otherwise has bound 2 and coercivity 1, but F_h(w)=3w/2 has no solution. Added explicit sesquilinearity (real bilinearity) with matching slot conventions for both forms. Lax–Milgram now applies to the closed finite-dimensional subspace, and first-slot linearity licenses the residual identity; triangle inequality and the nonzero-error division give the unchanged estimate.

The displayed supremum omitted V_h={0}, although A2 imports the zero convention from the framework. Made that convention explicit. Review also found that the extension definition only imposes agreement and a bound, not sesquilinearity: the nonlinear c(v)vw example from first Strang is permitted when V=V_h=R and defeats existence. Explicitly required exact and extended forms to be sesquilinear, with matching slot conventions. Their restriction now licenses discrete Lax–Milgram and the first-slot residual decomposition; division, triangle inequality, infimum, and uniform consequences then hold, including the zero space.

The two closed-cell formulas assigned different midpoint values, e.g. phi_L had values 1 and 0 at 1/2. Specified disjoint cells [0,1/2] and (1/2,1], using the left midpoint value. This nonfatal representative ambiguity affects neither integral nor cellwise slope after the convention is supplied. Verified the norm formulas 2(c_L^2+c_R^2) and (c_L^2+c_R^2)/6, common space X_h=L2, bilinear extension, bounded loads, Fubini identity F(h)=integral h(1-3t^2) on mean-zero V, and residual 1/2-3/4=-1/4 with norm sqrt(2). Countable Choice is now explicit in the Example as already required by its Given block.
